evidence.reason: This is a defense-in-depth hardening request, not a demonstrated implementation defect. The supplied region shows a deliberate tool policy (allow read/edit/bash; sandbox 'none') justified at lines 685–689 as the network-needing op's only honest request under the frozen policy; the op needs bash for commit/fetch. Existing intended behavior already forbids the worker pushing — the rendered prompt states 'do not run git push (any form)' — and the sanctioned publication path runs through the merge seam behind the scan gate, while current contract items 12/17 enforce the fail-closed denylist on the exact PR head so anything that lands is caught before merge. The finding itself concedes 'no code change is proposed here' and 'the inspected code does not establish that mechanism,' i.e. it proposes enlarging protection scope (a tool-level git push block) rather than fixing a concrete bug. The module-header vs prompt contradiction is a comment/documentation nit, not a functional defect. An opportunity to harden prompt-level prohibition into tool-level enforcement does not itself establish a current obligation.
